title: Gradient spec line word drop
summary: One short spec line on white, each word dropping from slightly above while fading in, staggered about a quarter second apart, the whole line painted in a cool-to-lime gradient, then a long calm hold.
use_when: A chapter title or single feature claim inside a premium announcement
Naming one hero spec (resolution, battery, speed) in three words or fewer
Opening a silent product reel on a light, restrained brand
Inserting a calm text beat between UI or device shots

look.type_style: medium-bold grotesk, sentence case, normal tracking, cap height about 9 % of frame height, one line centred, horizontal gradient fill slate teal to lime across the line

structure.shot: white frame, then one centred spec line of 3 words (number, then two words) in a left-to-right cool-to-lime gradient
structure.camera: static (line position and width identical in sheet-01 cells 7 to 15)
structure.motion: empty f0 to f12 (±0.25 s); per word fade-in with a drop of about 0.5 em from above, easings.outQuint ~15 fr (±0.25 s), stagger ~8 fr (±0.25 s); last word settled by f53 (±0.25 s); hold 67 fr to the end

params.brand: any brand.json: display font, bg, two or three accent stops for the gradient
params.content.line: one spec line, 2-4 words, optionally led by a number
params.content.gradient: colour stops left to right across the line (default brand muted to accent)
params.timing.lead: empty frames before the first word (default 12)
params.timing.enter: frames of each word's fade and drop (default 15)
params.aspect: 16:9 | 1:1 | 4:5 | 9:16; the line caps at 84 % of width
params.fps: composition fps (default 30); timing scales with it

notes: Measured from 4 fps sheets only (±0.25 s). Words come down into place, not up: in sheet-01 cells 2 and 3 each later word sits higher than the previous one, matching a drop from above. No clip mask is visible (faded words are drawn above the baseline unclipped), so the catalogue hints mask-wipe and slide-push are not used; there is no horizontal slide. The gradient is fixed to the line, not per word. Blur in the entrance is not measurable at this resolution; blur-in is the closest vocabulary entry (BlurIn blurDrop with a longer stagger). Proposed term: gradient-fill. sfx planned by the glue rule, not measured (reference is silent).
